<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Preserve CohereASR runtime FP16 relative-position bias buffers when loading FP32 checkpoint tensors. Fixes #54377; refreshed against main `c5f8adc0` after #55190.

## Claims

- Remove the loading-time buffer dtype override; keep the normal weight loader and shared attention-buffer references.
- Move the existing regression into `tests/models/multimodal/test_cohere_asr.py`, as requested by @ekagra-ranjan, retaining upstream fusion and audio-token tests.

## Validation

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/test_cohere_asr.py -v` — **6 passed**.
- The migrated bias-loading regression fails against unmodified main production code (`float32` rather than `float16`) and passes with this fix.
- `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/cohere_asr.py tests/models/multimodal/test_cohere_asr.py` — **passed**, including mypy and Buildkite test tethering.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- No new Turing/H100 model or WER evaluation ran on this host: CUDA cannot initialize (driver 12.4; installed torch CUDA 13.0). Earlier H100 testing reported by the reviewer is prior-head evidence in this discussion, not a fresh result.

## Details

The custom `param.data.to(loaded_weight.dtype)` replaced the runtime FP16 buffer with an FP32 tensor before loading, overriding `--dtype` and leaving attention with mixed dtypes. The normal loader already casts checkpoint values into the existing destination dtype.

Duplicate check: re-read #54377 and searched open PRs by issue number and CohereASR/pos_bias; no competing open fix was found. #55190 is a merged attention optimization, whose tests are preserved. Current main still contains the offending conversion. This PR has been open since 2026-08-30.

AI assistance was used for this refresh and validation. Commits include Signed-off-by and OpenAI Codex attribution; human review of the updated diff and remaining hardware validation are still required.

nodes.body:
Hi @ActiveSky - thanks for the PR! 

The issue was that the `pos_bias` variables were being casted to the dtype of the original weight rather than the runtime type decided by `--dtype`. A direct fix would be to remove [this](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/bd575a0d0bdf482557648e5278bbba98b6a939b9/vllm/model_executor/models/cohere_asr.py#L1820-L1828) block of code during weight loading. I removed it and tried on H100 and it worked and the existing tests WER tests passed for cohere ASR. 

Can you do that instead in this PR and confirm it works on your Turing GPU?

Hi @ekagra-ranjan, thank you for the detailed diagnosis and for testing the alternative on H100. We checked the loading path and confirmed that the custom pos_bias conversion changes the shared relative-position bias buffers to the checkpoint dtype, overriding the runtime dtype. We updated this PR to remove that conversion and restored the original attention additions. We also added a regression test covering FP32 checkpoint values loaded into FP16 runtime buffers and a corresponding attention forward pass.

The focused test, .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/test_cohere_asr.py -v, passed, and the project pre-commit checks passed. The update is in commit fee8e03596c6031247ecb8d557bf61ff5369c9d0. Could you please take another look when convenient? Thank you again for your guidance.
@ActiveSky - after #55190 is merged, could you move the testfile you created in this PR to `tests/models/multimodal/test_cohere_asr.py` before we merge this PR?

Hi @ekagra-ranjan, thank you for the follow-up suggestion. We’ve noted it and will keep an eye on #55190. Once #55190 is merged, we’ll update this PR to move the test file to `tests/models/multimodal/test_cohere_asr.py` as recommended, before proceeding with the merge. Thank you again for your guidance.

Hi @ekagra-ranjan @AndreasKaratzas @DarkLight1337 @ywang96, #55190 has merged, and I have now merged main `c5f8adc0` and moved the regression into the existing `tests/models/multimodal/test_cohere_asr.py`, as requested, preserving the upstream tests. The refresh is signed/signed off with AI attribution, and I ran the current PR checklist.

Validation: **6 tests passed**, pre-commit passed. The same bias regression fails on main (`float32` instead of runtime `float16`) and passes here. I could not rerun GPU/WER evaluation on this host, and the description states that limit.

This PR has been open since **August 30**, and the loading-time dtype override is still present on main, so the reported FP16 startup failure still has an actionable fix. Could you please take another look at the refreshed diff and help advance the required review/CI steps when possible? Thank you for your earlier guidance.

Hi @DarkLight1337, thank you for reviewing this PR and enabling auto-merge.

I checked the [only failed job in Buildkite #95051](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95051#01a13e52-a33e-43e0-a239-28b6103d7c45) at head `b09c47bf3f`. The failure is `test_derender_parity.py::test_stream_parity_reasoning`, using `DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B`: the replayed derender output includes a trailing `<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>` that the coupled streaming output omits. That test phase finished with 100 passed and 1 failed.

The production change here is confined to `CohereASRModel.load_weights()`, which this model does not use, plus its regression test. This looks unrelated based on the code paths and logs, but I have not reproduced it on an unmodified build at the same base commit, so I cannot confirm that it is a pre-existing or flaky failure. Pre-commit and DCO passed on this head.

If you agree that the failure is unrelated and repository policy permits, would you please consider merging this PR manually? Otherwise, I am happy to wait for a retry of the failed shard or provide further investigation. Thank you again for your time and help.

Hi @DarkLight1337 @AndreasKaratzas @ywang96, thank you again for the approval and auto-merge setup. Following up because this PR has been open since August 30: the CohereASR attention-bias dtype conversion is still present on main `7b77ed581d`, so the FP16 fix remains relevant.

The remaining CI obstacle is still the reasoning-stream parity failure in Buildkite #95051 discussed above. Its DeepSeek/Qwen code path appears separate from this CohereASR-only change, but I have not established a same-base control and cannot call it proven unrelated or flaky. Could you please take another look and advise whether to retry that shard or what further evidence is needed to proceed with merging under the project's rules? Thank you for helping advance this.

✅ Triggered [Buildkite CI #98940](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/98940) for commit `fe2af32e2cc7`, running 1 failed step(s) from [Buildkite CI #95051](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95051).

files.patch:
@@ -5,12 +5,15 @@
 
 import pytest
 import torch
+from torch import nn
 
 from vllm.config import SpeechToTextConfig
 from vllm.model_executor.models.cohere_asr import (
     CohereAsrForConditionalGeneration,
+    CohereASRModel,
     RelPositionMultiHeadAttention,
 )
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_default_torch_dtype
 
 
 class _ReferenceRelPositionMultiHeadAttention(RelPositionMultiHeadAttention):
@@ -88,3 +91,42 @@ def test_get_num_audio_tokens_streaming_estimate(audio_duration_s, expected_toke
     )
 
     assert got == expected_tokens
+
+
+class _CohereASRWeightLoadingModel(CohereASRModel):
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        nn.Module.__init__(self)
+        self.register_buffer("pos_bias_u", torch.zeros(2, 2))
+        self.register_buffer("pos_bias_v", torch.zeros(2, 2))
+        self.attention = RelPositionMultiHeadAttention(
+            n_head=2,
+            n_feat=4,
+            pos_bias_u=self.pos_bias_u,
+            pos_bias_v=self.pos_bias_v,
+        )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.cpu_test
+def test_load_weights_preserves_runtime_bias_dtype() -> None:
+    with set_default_torch_dtype(torch.float16):
+        model = _CohereASRWeightLoadingModel()
+
+    loaded_weight = torch.ones_like(model.pos_bias_u, dtype=torch.float32)
+    model.load_weights([("pos_bias_u", loaded_weight), ("pos_bias_v", loaded_weight)])
+
+    assert model.pos_bias_u.dtype == torch.float16
+    assert model.pos_bias_v.dtype == torch.float16
+    assert model.attention.pos_bias_u.dtype == torch.float16
+    assert model.attention.pos_bias_v.dtype == torch.float16
+    torch.testing.assert_close(model.pos_bias_u, loaded_weight.half())
+
+    output = model.attention(
+        query=torch.randn(1, 3, 4, dtype=torch.float16),
+        key=torch.randn(1, 3, 4, dtype=torch.float16),
+        value=torch.randn(1, 3, 4, dtype=torch.float16),
+        mask=None,
+        pos_emb=torch.randn(1, 5, 4, dtype=torch.float16),
+    )
+
+    assert output.dtype == torch.float16
+    assert output.shape == (1, 3, 4)

@@ -1845,16 +1845,6 @@ def load_weights(self, weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> set[str]:
                 param = params_dict[name]
                 weight_loader = getattr(param, "weight_loader", default_weight_loader)
 
-                # Convert buffer dtype to match loaded weight for pos_bias tensors
-                if "pos_bias" in name and param.dtype != loaded_weight.dtype:
-                    logger.info(
-                        "Converting buffer %s dtype from %s to %s for loading.",
-                        name,
-                        param.dtype,
-                        loaded_weight.dtype,
-                    )
-                    param.data = param.data.to(loaded_weight.dtype)
-
                 weight_loader(param, loaded_weight)
             loaded_params.add(name)
         return loaded_params
